nodes.label: PUT /api/v1/tasks/{id}/progress
nodes.rationale: Edge case defined: when progress >= 100 the task status is automatically set to completed, keeping progress and status consistent server-side.

nodes.label: PUT /api/v1/tasks/{taskId}/checklist/{itemId}/toggle
nodes.rationale: Toggling a checklist item inverts is_completed and the task progress is recalculated from the checklist, making the checklist the source of truth for progress.

nodes.label: Premium Minimalism Aesthetic
nodes.rationale: Chosen to reduce cognitive load for housekeeping staff in high-pressure environments; prioritizes legibility and rapid information processing via whitespace and light-on-light layering, mirroring five-star hotel standards. All UI translated to Uzbek for local operational clarity.

nodes.label: Color Palette (Royal Blue anchor)
nodes.rationale: Royal Blue #1D4ED8 signals trust and professional rigor; strictly white background emphasizes a sterile, clean environment appropriate for hotel housekeeping.

nodes.label: Room Status Colors (Tozalangan/Tayyor/Jarayonda/Muammo/Tozalanishi kerak)
nodes.rationale: Status colors are functional signifiers, not decoration: orange for In Progress prevents management double-booking; red flags issues needing immediate attention; neutral gray marks the baseline pending state.

nodes.label: Inter Typography System
nodes.rationale: Inter chosen for exceptional mobile legibility and neutral systematic character; hierarchy leads with room number/primary task; Uzbek labels ensure immediate recognizability for staff.

nodes.label: Mobile-First Fluid Grid Layout
nodes.rationale: Designed for one-handed operation; 20px margins prevent accidental edge touches; 8px vertical rhythm; 48px minimum touch targets accommodate staff wearing gloves or moving quickly between rooms.

nodes.label: Soft Ambient Shadows Elevation
nodes.rationale: Depth via subtle shadows instead of heavy borders separates white cards from white background; active In Progress cards elevate to Level 2 to draw focus; modal blurs used sparingly to keep the user grounded in the room dashboard context.

nodes.label: Rounded Shape Language (16-20px radius)
nodes.rationale: High corner radius softens the industrial feel of hospitality software; pill-shaped badges are visually distinguished from structural cards.

nodes.label: Checklist Items Component
nodes.rationale: Large 24px checkbox and whole-row tap target chosen to facilitate rapid movement through room cleaning steps.

nodes.label: Material 3 Design Token System (Tailwind Config)
nodes.rationale: The page defines a full Material Design 3 color role vocabulary (primary, surface-container-*, on-surface-variant, error-container, etc.) plus typography and spacing scales inside tailwind.config so every UI element binds to semantic tokens rather than raw hex values, enabling dark mode via darkMode:'class' and consistent theming across the Housekeeping Pro design examples.

nodes.label: Notification Severity Color Coding
nodes.rationale: Each notification card uses a 4px left border and tinted icon chip whose color role encodes the notification type: error (red) for critical emergencies with action buttons (BORISH/RAD ETISH), primary (blue) for new task assignments, secondary for accepted/resolved items shown at reduced opacity, tertiary (orange) for inventory alerts, and outline-variant (gray, faded) for low-priority system messages — letting workers triage by glance.

nodes.label: Notification Swipe Micro-interaction Script
nodes.rationale: A small touch-event script translates cards left on swipe (visual only, snapping back on touchend) plus a scale(0.98) active state, giving a native-app dismiss affordance without any real dismissal logic in this static prototype.

nodes.label: Notifications Screen Mockup (Screenshot)
nodes.rationale: Rendered mobile mockup of the Uzbek-language notifications screen for hotel housekeeping staff: avatar + GoHotel Service header, 'Bildirishnomalar' list of five severity-coded notification cards (critical water-leak emergency with action buttons, new task, accepted problem, inventory, shift-ending), a decorative bell illustration promo block, and a five-item floating bottom navigation with the Xabarlar tab active.
